info.name: javascript-calc load test
info.description:
RAM / swap-thrash root-cause test for a 512MB plan (or single-node vs master-node comparison).

Setup:
1. Import this collection.
2. Edit the collection variable `base_url` (Collection > Variables) to your deployed URL, e.g. https://javascript-calc-master-xxxx.kuberns.site (no trailing slash).
3. Set `BOOT_DATASET_MB` env var on the deployed resource to size the app's boot-time baseline footprint (default 40MB) — simulates a real app's cold-start memory (loaded dataset + in-memory index), not an idle process.
4. Baseline: Send `stats` once right after boot, note rssMB (boot footprint) + peakRssMB + uptimeSec.
5. Load: open Runner > Performance tab, pick the `work` request, set Virtual Users (10 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100 -> 200 ...) and run for several minutes (real drift shows up over time, not seconds).
6. Watch error % in Postman. Re-send `stats` to read peakRssMB and uptimeSec.
   - error % climbing above 0 = concurrency it can't survive.
   - uptimeSec dropping back near 0 = container OOM-killed & restarted = hard breaking point.
   - On the box itself, watch `free -m` for Swap used climbing while load average stays low = swap-thrash, not clean OOM.
7. Repeat identically against the other architecture's URL and compare.

Each `work` request does a real outbound network call + CPU hashing + a per-request allocation that's released after response (GC-eligible, not a permanent leak) — this simulates genuine user traffic, not an artificial runaway. Dial pressure with the `work` query params: mb (MB per request), hold (ms in-flight), cpu (CPU passes). Live RAM ~= virtualUsers x mb while requests overlap.

request.description: Current + peak RAM of the app process and uptime. peakRssMB = how high RAM climbed. If uptimeSec suddenly resets near 0, the container was OOM-killed & restarted under load.

exec: // Surface the key numbers in the Postman test results + console.
console.log('RAM now=' + body.rssMB + 'MB  peak=' + body.peakRssMB + 'MB  uptime=' + body.uptimeSec + 's');

query.description: MB of real RAM allocated per request
ms the request stays in-flight (raises overlap/pressure)
CPU passes over the buffer per request

request.description: Allocates mb MB, does cpu CPU passes, holds hold ms, then responds. Run this via Runner > Performance with rising Virtual Users to find the breaking point. Each response also reports rssMB.
No-work liveness endpoint. Use as a control: if /ping stays fast/200 while /work fails, the failure is work/RAM-driven, not the server being down.
